title: Watchtower Incident Response
intro: Watchtower runs the platform every other desk in this curriculum sits on. Telemetry streams in all day; thresholds decide what becomes an alert; alerts page humans; runbooks act; postmortems tune the thresholds. This is automation about automation. You are going to build the nervous system: detect a threshold crossing, classify it, page a person or just watch, follow the runbook, tell users the truth, and close the loop with a postmortem that edits the thresholds. Then it meets an alert storm, a runbook that does not match reality, and a page nobody answers.

world.oneLiner: Watchtower keeps the platform alive: telemetry becomes alerts, alerts become incidents, incidents page people, runbooks resolve them, and postmortems tune the thresholds so it happens less.

roles.name: On-call Engineer
roles.does: First responder: is paged, acknowledges, follows the runbook.

roles.name: Incident Commander
roles.does: Owns severe incidents, and is paged when the on-call does not answer.

roles.name: Service Owner
roles.does: Owns each service's alert thresholds and hears the tuning proposals.

roles.name: SRE Lead
roles.does: Owns the runbooks and the monthly reliability report; hears when a runbook step did not match reality.

roles.name: Status Page
roles.does: An output, not a person: where users are told what is happening.

roles.name: Engineering DL
roles.does: The distribution list that receives the reliability report.

world.deliverable: a postmortem for every incident, and the monthly reliability report
world.clock: Every minute: telemetry samples arrive and are checked against the thresholds. During an incident: responders report each runbook step as they take it. Month end: postmortems are assembled, the report goes to Engineering, and the thresholds get their proposals.
world.stakes: Get it wrong and forty alerts page one engineer forty times, a page goes unanswered while customers wait, or a runbook that no longer matches the system is followed to the letter.

sources.label: Telemetry
sources.description: One sample per service per metric per minute: latency in ms, errors in percent.

sources.label: Responder Actions
sources.description: A responder reporting a runbook step: done, deviated (with why), or resolve.

stores.label: Alert Thresholds
stores.description: Per service and metric: the limit that trips an alert, and the impact and scope a crossing implies. Versioned, because incidents edit them.

stores.label: Severity Matrix
stores.description: Impact x scope -> severity, and whether that severity pages a human.

stores.label: Runbook Library
stores.description: Per service: the numbered steps a responder follows.

stores.label: Alert Events
stores.description: Every threshold crossing, as it happened.

stores.label: Incidents
stores.description: One row per incident: service, metric, severity, who was paged, how many alerts it absorbed, and when it was resolved.

stores.label: Watch Log
stores.description: Alerts below the paging band: recorded, not paged.

stores.label: Runbook Executions
stores.description: Every runbook step a responder reported, against what the runbook said.

stores.label: Runbook Deviations
stores.description: Steps where reality did not match the runbook. The runbook's to-do list.

stores.label: Postmortems
stores.description: One per resolved incident: timeline, impact, response, actions.

stores.label: Action Items
stores.description: Tracked commitments from postmortems, each with an owner.

stores.label: Tuning Proposals
stores.description: Threshold edits proposed by this month's incidents.

flows.name: Month end
flows.description: Runs at month end: postmortems, report, tuning.

days.label: Month 1 - one clean incident
days.description: API latency crosses its limit at minute 10 and the on-call answers the page. Web errors tick just over their limit - worth watching, not worth waking anyone. The runbook works and the incident is resolved at minute 32.

responder-actions.note: checked the dashboard: one upstream slow

runbook-library.action: check the latency dashboard for the slow upstream

days.label: Month 2 - the storm, and a runbook that lies
days.description: Database errors cross the limit five minutes in a row. The on-call answers, follows the runbook, and finds step 2 does not work any more: restarting the replica did nothing; failing over did.

responder-actions.note: restart did not clear it; failed over to the standby instead

days.label: Month 3 - the page nobody answers
days.description: API latency trips again at minute 5. The page goes out. The on-call's phone is on a plane. Nobody acknowledges.

builds.title: Detect
builds.brief: A sample over its threshold becomes an alert event; everything else is noise.
builds.goal: Every minute, every service reports every metric. Almost all of it is fine. The Alert Thresholds table says, per service and metric, the value that means trouble. Compare each sample with its threshold; at or over it, record an alert event.
builds.outcome: Every sample at or over its threshold is in Alert Events with the limit it crossed; nothing else is.
constraints: Look the threshold up by service AND metric.
At or over the limit trips.
Attach the threshold as threshold - the next build reads its impact and scope.

hints.question: Four samples arrived. How many should wake anyone?
hints.nudge: A Lookup on Alert Thresholds where service = service and metric = metric (threshold); a Condition value >= threshold.limit: YES lane Transform limit = threshold.limit; Store into Alert Events.
steps: Connect the Trigger to Telemetry.
Add a Lookup on Alert Thresholds where service = service and metric = metric. Name it threshold.
Add a Condition: value >= threshold.limit (compare to the field).
YES lane: Transform limit = threshold.limit; Store into Alert Events. Run it.

checks.why: A detector that fails is a platform nobody is watching.
checks.label: The telemetry flow runs without failing

checks.why: 850 ms against a 500 ms limit: an alert.
checks.label: T-101 (api latency 850) is an alert

checks.why: 2.5 percent against 2: over, if only just.
checks.label: T-102 (web errors 2.5%) is an alert

checks.why: The other two samples are noise; recording them would bury the signal.
checks.label: Only 2 alerts from 4 samples

builds.title: Page, or watch
builds.brief: Classify each alert with the matrix; page a human above the band, log the rest.
builds.goal: Not every alert is worth waking someone. The threshold says what impact and scope a crossing implies; the Severity Matrix turns those into a severity and says whether it pages. In the alert lane: open an incident, and either page the On-call Engineer (capturing the acknowledgement, and telling the Status Page) or log it in the Watch Log.
builds.outcome: Every alert opens an incident with its severity; paging severities page the On-call Engineer and tell the Status Page; the rest go to the Watch Log.
constraints: incidentId = service + '-' + metric + '-' + minute.
Severity comes from the matrix by the threshold's impact AND scope.
Page = a Send to the On-call Engineer and an Approval capturing the acknowledgement; record pagedTo.
Below the band: Watch Log, no page.

hints.question: Web errors at 2.5 percent, affecting some users. Is that worth a 3 AM phone call?
hints.nudge: In the alert lane: Lookup Severity Matrix where impact = threshold.impact and scope = threshold.scope (sev); Transform incidentId, severity = sev.severity, status = 'open', alertCount = 1; Condition sev.page == true: YES lane Send to On-call Engineer, Approval from On-call Engineer, Transform pagedTo = 'On-call Engineer', Send to Status Page; NO lane Store into Watch Log. Then Store into Incidents (add or replace by incidentId).
steps: In the alert YES lane, after the Alert Events store: Lookup Severity Matrix where impact = threshold.impact and scope = threshold.scope. Name it sev.
Transform: incidentId = concat(service, '-', metric, '-', minute), severity = sev.severity, status = 'open', alertCount = 1.

Condition: sev.page == true. YES lane: Send to On-call Engineer ('{{severity}} {{service}} {{metric}} {{value}}{{unit}}'); Approval from On-call Engineer about '{{incidentId}}'; Transform pagedTo = 'On-call Engineer'; Send to Status Page ('Investigating {{service}} {{metric}}'). NO lane: Store into Watch Log.
After that Condition: Store into Incidents, add or replace if it exists, same row when incidentId. Run it.

builds.title: Follow the runbook
builds.brief: Record each step a responder takes against the runbook, and close the incident on resolve.
builds.goal: Responders report each runbook step as they take it. Record each one next to what the runbook said the step was. When the step is resolve, close the incident: status resolved, the minute, and how long it took - then tell the Status Page.
builds.outcome: Every responder action is in Runbook Executions with the runbook's action; resolve closes the incident with resolvedMinute and mttr and tells the Status Page.
constraints: Look the incident up; the runbook step is by the incident's service AND the step number.
mttr = resolve minute minus the incident's minute.
Update the incident row; never add one.

hints.question: At minute 32 the on-call says it is fixed. What should the incident row say, and who else should know?
hints.nudge: Trigger on Responder Actions; Lookup Incidents by incidentId (incident); Lookup Runbook Library where service = incident.service and step = step (runbook); Transform action = runbook.action; Store into Runbook Executions; Condition step == resolve: YES lane Transform status = 'resolved', resolvedMinute = minute, mttr = minute - incident.minute; Store into Incidents (update by incidentId); Send to Status Page.
steps: Open the Runbook steps flow and connect it to Responder Actions.
Lookup Incidents where incidentId = incidentId (incident); Lookup Runbook Library where service = incident.service and step = step (runbook).
Transform action = runbook.action; Store into Runbook Executions.

Condition: step == resolve. YES lane: Transform status = 'resolved', resolvedMinute = minute, mttr = minute - incident.minute; Store into Incidents, update the existing row by incidentId; Send to Status Page ('Resolved {{incident.service}}'). Run it.

checks.why: A lost step is a timeline with a hole.
checks.label: The runbook flow runs without failing

checks.why: Two steps and a resolve, all on record.
checks.label: Three actions recorded for api-latency-10

checks.label: Step 2 is recorded against the runbook's action

checks.why: Tripped at 10, resolved at 32: 22 minutes.
checks.label: api-latency-10 is resolved, mttr 22

checks.why: Users are told when it is over, too.
checks.label: The Status Page says resolved

builds.title: Postmortem and report
builds.brief: At month end, write a postmortem per resolved incident and send the reliability report.
builds.goal: Each resolved incident gets a postmortem: what tripped, how severe, how long, which steps were taken. The month gets a report: incidents and total time to resolve. Loop over the resolved incidents, gather each one's steps, write it up, then report to Engineering and archive.
builds.outcome: Every resolved incident has a postmortem with its steps; Engineering receives the report; a copy is archived.
constraints: Only resolved incidents get a postmortem.
stepsTaken = the number of executions for the incident.
The report counts incidents and totals mttr.

hints.question: What does the SRE Lead want to read a month later about minute 10?
hints.nudge: Lookup Incidents all where status = 'resolved' (resolved); For each: Lookup Runbook Executions all where incidentId = incidentId (steps); Transform stepsTaken = len(steps); Store into Postmortems (add or replace by incidentId); Transform status = 'closed'; Store into Incidents (update by incidentId). After: Transform incidents = len(resolved), totalMttr = sum(resolved, 'mttr'); Compose; Send to Engineering DL; Store into Reliability Archive.
steps: Open the Month end flow. Lookup Incidents, all rows where status = 'resolved'. Name it resolved. For each over resolved.

Inside: Lookup Runbook Executions, all rows where incidentId = incidentId (steps); Transform stepsTaken = len(steps); Store into Postmortems, add or replace by incidentId; Transform status = 'closed'; Store into Incidents, update the existing row by incidentId, so next month does not write it again.
After the loop: Transform incidents = len(resolved), totalMttr = sum(resolved, 'mttr'). Compose report with the counts and {{#each resolved}}- {{incidentId}} {{severity}} {{mttr}} min{{/each}}.
Send to Engineering DL with {{report}}; Store into Reliability Archive.

builds.title: Close the loop
builds.brief: Every postmortem proposes a threshold review, with an owner.
builds.goal: Incidents edit thresholds - that is the whole loop. For each resolved incident, create an action item for the Service Owner to review the threshold that tripped, and a tuning proposal that shows the limit, the peak value seen, and how many alerts it absorbed. Tell the Service Owner.
builds.outcome: Every resolved incident produces an action item owned by the Service Owner and a tuning proposal, and the Service Owner is told.
constraints: The action item's owner is the Service Owner; dueDay = 14.
The proposal carries the threshold's current limit.

hints.question: The curriculum started with someone setting a threshold. Who sets them now?
hints.nudge: Inside the loop: Lookup Alert Thresholds where service = service and metric = metric (threshold); Transform item = concat('review ', service, ' ', metric, ' threshold'), owner = 'Service Owner', dueDay = 14, limit = threshold.limit; Store into Action Items; Store into Tuning Proposals; Send to Service Owner.
steps: Inside the loop, after the Incidents update: Lookup Alert Thresholds where service = service and metric = metric (threshold).
Transform item = concat('review ', service, ' ', metric, ' threshold'), owner = 'Service Owner', dueDay = 14, limit = threshold.limit.
Store into Action Items; Store into Tuning Proposals; Send to Service Owner ('Review {{service}} {{metric}} limit {{limit}}: {{severity}}, {{mttr}} min'). Run it.

checks.why: A commitment with a name and a date.
checks.label: An action item for api-latency-10, owned by the Service Owner

checks.why: The proposal names the limit that tripped.
checks.label: A tuning proposal for api latency (limit 500)

checks.why: The threshold's owner decides; the flow only proposes.

builds.title: Month 2: the storm
builds.brief: Five alerts in five minutes are one incident, not five pages.
builds.goal: Database errors crossed the limit five minutes running. Run your Month 1 flow: five incidents, five pages, one engineer. An alert for a service and metric that already has an open incident belongs to that incident: count it there and stop.
builds.outcome: Repeated alerts attach to the open incident (alertCount grows); one incident, one page.
constraints: An open incident for the same service and metric absorbs the alert.
alertCount counts every alert absorbed.
Nothing else is paged or created.

Condition: open exists. YES lane: Transform incidentId = open.incidentId, alertCount = open.alertCount + 1, minute = open.minute; Store into Incidents, update the existing row by incidentId; Stop.
Run again.

builds.title: Month 2: the runbook that lies
builds.brief: A step that did not work is a deviation: log it and tell the runbook's owner.
builds.goal: Step 2 says restart the replica. The on-call did, and it did nothing; failing over fixed it. Run your flow: the step is recorded as 'deviated' and nobody hears. A deviation is the runbook telling you it is wrong. Log it where the SRE Lead will see it, and tell them.
builds.outcome: Every deviated step is in Runbook Deviations with the responder's note, and the SRE Lead is told.
constraints: A deviation is anything reported as deviated.
Keep the responder's note - it is the fix.

steps: Run first and read A-202 in the run.
After the Runbook Executions store, add a Condition: outcome == deviated. YES lane: Store into Runbook Deviations; Send to SRE Lead ('Runbook {{incident.service}} step {{step}} deviated: {{note}}').
Run again.

checks.why: The runbook's owner has to hear it lied.

checks.label: Only the deviated step is logged

builds.title: Month 3: nobody answers
builds.brief: An unacknowledged page climbs the ladder to the Incident Commander.
builds.goal: API latency trips at minute 5, the page goes out, and nobody acknowledges. Run your Month 2 flow: the incident says paged to the On-call Engineer, and that is where it stays. When the acknowledgement does not come, page the Incident Commander and say so on the incident.
builds.outcome: An unacknowledged page pages the Incident Commander; the incident records pagedTo = Incident Commander.
constraints: The On-call Engineer is still paged first.
Not acknowledged is anything but acknowledged.
pagedTo names the last person paged.
